subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec promise inline PowerShell `$...` command fidelity, adopt the one-shot explicit approval direction from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322, or document script-file/direct-command limitations instead?
rationale: The source-backed failure sits on a command execution approval boundary, and the acceptable fix depends on maintainer intent about Windows command fidelity versus conservative approval/security behavior.

options.title: Hold For Proven PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and require real Windows/Gateway proof before deciding whether the linked one-shot approval fix is the canonical solution.

options.title: Document The Limitation
options.body: Document that inline PowerShell `$...` payloads are not guaranteed and recommend `.ps1` files or direct non-shell commands as the supported path.

options.title: Sponsor Alternate Runtime Fix
options.body: Ask for a different owner-approved execution-path change if maintainers want literal inline PowerShell fidelity without the PR's approval semantics.

recommendation.title: Hold For Proven PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require real Windows/Gateway proof before deciding whether the linked one-shot approval fix is the canonical solution.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily affects the Windows command authorization and approval-planning surface introduced in the Tree-sitter command planner work.
